Aspiration Aspiration occurs when ﬂ uid is 
inspired into the lungs. Patients who are sedated, 
who have an endotracheal tube (a tube that allows 
oxygen into the lungs of patients receiving mechani-
cal ventilation), or who have diﬃ  culty swallowing
are at risk for aspiration. It is a potentially serious
condition that may result in pneumonia or even
death. To avoid aspiration, it is important that the 
patient’s head be elevated higher than her or his 
stomach, or at an angle of >30 degrees, during feed-
ing. Common practices to assess for aspiration such 
as blue dye or glucose oxidase are no longer recom-
